question: If S-104's next RM-221 shipment ships two weeks late, when will DC-EAST run out of Lacrivia, when will supply recover there, and which customers get supply first under our allocation rules?
answer:
**Answer:** DC-EAST is already out of Lacrivia. If S-104's next RM-221 shipment ships two weeks late, the earliest the replacement supply reaches DC-EAST is about **10 Dec 2026**. When it arrives, the three **Tier A health systems get it first (Riverbend, Oak Hollow, Northfield)**, then the two Tier B systems (Clearview, Sunridge), then everyone else in proportion to their prescriptions.

**1. When DC-EAST runs out: it already has (about 26–27 Sep)**

| Pack | On hand (25 Sep snapshot) | Safety stock | Avg daily shipments, last 28 days | Days of supply | Stock-out |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 5 mL (FG-1001) | 46 | 471 | 36.7 | 1.3 | about 26 Sep |
| Lacrivia 10 mL (FG-1002) | 34 | 233 | 15.1 | 2.3 | about 27 Sep |

Both packs have been below safety stock since 11 Sep. The late shipment doesn't change the stock-out date; it makes the outage longer.

**2. When supply recovers: about 10 Dec 2026**
- The next open order is **PO005791**: 4,200 units of RM-221, promised to ship 7 Oct. Two weeks late means it ships **21 Oct**.
- It then takes **50 days** to become finished goods at the DC: 6 days transit to the premix supplier (S-201), 10 days to make, test and ship the premix to the plant, 15 days through the bulk and fill stages, then 19 days for packing, quality release (including the 14-day sterility test) and transit to the DC.
- So supply reaches DC-EAST around **10 Dec**, against about 26 Nov if the order shipped on time.
- That is an outage of roughly **75 days**, with about **3,900 units of demand not covered** (about 2,750 of the 5 mL and 1,130 of the 10 mL). The two-week delay alone adds about 725 units.
- **There's no backup supplier.** S-104 is the only qualified source of RM-221; the alternate, S-131, isn't qualified. The premix (CMP-310) also has a single source, S-201.
- **There's no company substitute.** Cyclosporine 0.05% (FG-1003) uses the same RM-221 and premix chain, so under the substitution rule there is no approved company substitute. Medical Affairs guides therapeutic alternatives.

**3. Who gets supply first**
Units go in contract-tier order, then to everyone else in proportion to their last 13 weeks of Lacrivia prescriptions. Only clinics in DC-EAST's states (NY, NJ, PA, MA, FL, GA, NC, OH) are counted; total is 5,170 prescriptions.

| Priority | Customer | Prescriptions, last 13 weeks (DC-EAST states) | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 – Tier A | Riverbend Health System | 836 | 16.2% |
| 1 – Tier A | Oak Hollow Health System | 708 | 13.7% |
| 1 – Tier A | Northfield Health System | 533 | 10.3% |
| 2 – Tier B | Clearview Health System (contract ends 31 Dec 2026) | 530 | 10.3% |
| 2 – Tier B | Sunridge Health System | 428 | 8.3% |
| 3 – Proportional | All other customers | 2,135 | 41.3% |

Largest shares of the proportional group:

| Customer | Share of the group |
|---|---|
| Brightwater Health System | 19.4% |
| Stonegate Health System | 15.0% |
| Sunridge Vision Associates 20 | 9.3% |
| Willow Creek Health System | 8.8% |
| Harbor Point Vision Associates 2 | 6.5% |
| Highland Vision Associates 26 | 6.2% |

13 smaller independent clinics make up the rest.

Some clinics share a name with a contracted health system: Sunridge Vision Associates 20, Clearview Vision Associates 13, Riverbend Vision Associates 16 and Northfield Vision Associates 19. They have no parent account, so they **don't** get that system's tier and sit in the proportional group.

**Caveats**
- I found no data on work in progress or plant schedules. RM-221 shipped in September (PO000360 and PO000362–364) could turn into finished goods earlier, roughly 29 Oct to 13 Nov using the same 50-day lead time. Check with the plant before you rely on 10 Dec.
- Clearview's Tier B contract expires 31 Dec. If recovery slips past that, check its tier again.
- Moving stock in from other DCs needs Supply Planning approval. I didn't check stock at DC-CENTRAL or DC-WEST.

**Sources and definitions**
- **Data:** Fabric tables PURCH_ORD (purchase orders), DC_INV (DC inventory) and WHSLR_SHIP (shipments to wholesalers); Snowflake prescription, prescriber and account tables (RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY, CORE.PRESCRIBER, CORE.ACCOUNT).
- **Knowledge-layer tools and reference sets:** the supply trace (`trace_supply_exposure`, S-104/RM-221) for which products are affected and single sourcing; `get_lead_times` (standard plant times) for the 50 days; the supply-contract and DC service-region reference lists.
- **Definitions:** days of supply as ratified (latest on-hand ÷ average daily shipments over 28 days).
- **Business rules applied:**
  - BR-LEAD-01: recovery only after every downstream stage completes.
  - BR-SUB-01: substitutes.
  - BR-ALLOC-01: allocation order.
  - BR-CUST-01: customer = top-level contracted account.
  - BR-REGION-01: accounts are served by the DC for their state.
- **Assumptions:**
  - "Next shipment" means PO005791, the earliest open order.
  - No other finished goods arrive at DC-EAST in the meantime.
  - Demand stays at the last-28-day rate.

sql.sql: SELECT PO_ID, SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, ORDER_DT, PROMISED_SHIP_DT, ACTUAL_SHIP_DT, QTY, STATUS FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD WHERE SUPPLIER_ID='S-104' AND MATERIAL_ID='RM-221' ORDER BY PROMISED_SHIP_DT DESC

SELECT m.MATERIAL_ID, m.MATERIAL_DESC, m.MATERIAL_TYP, m.PACK_SZ, x.NDC FROM dbo.MATERIAL m LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL_NDC_XREF x ON x.MATERIAL_ID=m.MATERIAL_ID WHERE m.MATERIAL_DESC LIKE '%acrivia%' OR m.MATERIAL_DESC LIKE '%yclosporine%'

SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, SNAPSHOT_DT, ON_HAND_UNITS, SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV WHERE DC_ID='DC-EAST' AND MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003') AND SNAPSHOT_DT >= '2026-08-15' ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID, SNAPSHOT_DT

SELECT MATERIAL_ID, COUNT(*) n, SUM(UNITS) units_28d, SUM(UNITS)/28.0 avg_daily, MIN(SHIP_DT) mn, MAX(SHIP_DT) mx FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP WHERE DC_ID='DC-EAST' AND MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003') AND SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-28,'2026-09-30') AND SHIP_DT <= '2026-09-30' GROUP BY MATERIAL_ID

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
rx AS (
SELECT c.ACCOUNT_ID clinic_id, c.STATE, COALESCE(gp.ACCOUNT_ID, par.ACCOUNT_ID, c.ACCOUNT_ID) top_id,
 r.PROD_NDC11, r.TRX_QTY
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r
JOIN wk ON r.WK_END_DT=wk.WK_END_DT
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p ON r.PRSCRBR_ME=p.PRSCRBR_ME
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT c ON p.ACCOUNT_ID=c.ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT par ON c.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID=par.ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT gp ON par.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID=gp.ACCOUNT_ID
WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110')
 AND c.STATE IN ('NY','NJ','PA','MA','FL','GA','NC','OH'))
SELECT rx.top_id, t.ACCOUNT_NM, t.ACCT_TYP, t.STATE top_state,
 SUM(TRX_QTY) trx13, SUM(CASE WHEN PROD_NDC11='99101010105' THEN TRX_QTY END) trx_5ml,
 SUM(CASE WHEN PROD_NDC11='99101010110' THEN TRX_QTY END) trx_10ml,
 COUNT(DISTINCT clinic_id) clinics, LISTAGG(DISTINCT rx.STATE, ',') states,
 SUM(SUM(TRX_QTY)) OVER () total_east
FROM rx JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT t ON rx.top_id=t.ACCOUNT_ID
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY trx13 DESC LIMIT 60
SELECT ACCOUNT_ID, ACCOUNT_NM, PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID, ACCT_TYP, STATE FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT WHERE ACCOUNT_ID IN ('AC00178','AC00171','AC00174','AC00177','AC00160','AC00184')
